title: Spaghetti Bolognese
description: A classic Italian pasta dish featuring slow-cooked Bolognese sauce made with beef and pork mince, San Marzano tomatoes, red wine, and milk, tossed with perfectly cooked spaghetti and finished with Parmigiano Reggiano.

ingredients.title: For the Bolognese Sauce
items: Beef mince (80% lean, freshly ground if possible) – 500 g
San Marzano tomatoes (canned, crushed by hand) – 400 g
Dry red wine (Chianti or Barolo preferred) – 250 ml
Sea salt & freshly ground black pepper – to taste

ingredients.title: For Finishing
items: Parmigiano Reggiano (24-month aged, freshly grated) – generous amount
Fresh flat-leaf parsley (finely chopped) – for garnish

instruction.title: Step 1 – Base Preparation
steps: Heat olive oil and butter in a wide, heavy-bottomed pan.
Sweat onion, carrot, celery, and garlic over medium-low heat until soft and translucent (about 10 minutes).

instruction.title: Step 2 – Browning the Meat
steps: Add beef and pork mince, season lightly, and cook until browned and caramelized.
Break into small crumbles, but avoid over-stirring—allow fond (browned bits) to form for depth of flavor.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Deglazing & Building Flavor
steps: Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes to caramelize.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up any browned bits.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Slow Cooking
steps: Add crushed San Marzano tomatoes, beef stock, milk, thyme, bay leaf, and nutmeg.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then lower heat.
Cook uncovered on very low heat for 2.5–3 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add a splash of stock if drying out.
Season with salt and pepper towards the end.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Pasta Cooking
steps: Cook spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until just al dente.
Reserve ½ cup of pasta water before draining.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Final Assembly
steps: Add spaghetti to the Bolognese sauce with a splash of pasta water.
Toss until the pasta is fully coated and glossy.
Rest for 1 minute off the heat to allow flavors to meld.

servingSuggestions.title: Plating & Presentation
items: Use a carving fork or tongs to twirl pasta into a neat mound in the center of a warm plate.
Spoon extra Bolognese sauce on top.
Garnish with a few parsley leaves and a drizzle of fine olive oil.

chefTips: Meat Balance: The mix of beef + pork creates depth and richness. Some chefs also add veal for delicacy.
Milk: Essential for softening the acidity of tomatoes and wine, giving a silky texture.
Slow Cooking: The hallmark of a true Bolognese. Flavors should meld into a deep, rich, almost sweet-savory sauce.
Wine Selection: Always cook with a wine you'd happily drink—its character defines the sauce.
Stock Quality: Homemade beef stock elevates the dish to restaurant-grade.
